articles.title: Container freight rates diverge as NYFI rises and Drewry WCI falls
articles.summary: Global container freight rates presented a mixed picture in the latest weekly assessments, with the NYSHEX Freight Index (NYFI) recording increases across all five monitored trade lanes while Drewry’s World Container Index (WCI) and the Freightos Baltic Index (FBX) declined. The contrasting movements were...
articles.body: Global container freight rates presented a mixed picture in the latest weekly assessments, with the NYSHEX Freight Index (NYFI) recording increases across all five monitored trade lanes while Drewry’s World Container Index (WCI) and the Freightos Baltic Index (FBX) declined. The contrasting movements were particularly evident on the Transpacific, where NYFI reported higher rates on both US coasts, while Drewry recorded notable decreases from Shanghai to Los Angeles and New York. Meanwhile, Chinese container freight benchmarks remained relatively stable, with the Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) and China Containerized Freight Index (CCFI) edging higher, while the Ningbo Containerized Freight Index (NCFI) declined. Chinese freight indexes show limited movement The SCFI increased approximately 0.16% to 3,687.35 points on 30 October, compared with 3,681.34 in the previous assessment. The CCFI also recorded a modest increase, rising 0.30% to 1,881.82 points from 1,876.27 a week earlier. The NCFI moved in the opposite direction, declining approximately 0.72% to 2,491.26 points, compared with 2,509.30 previously. Overall, the three Chinese composite indexes showed relatively limited weekly movements, suggesting broadly stable conditions across their respective market assessments. NYFI rises across all five trade lanes The NYFI assessment published on 30 October recorded positive movements across all five monitored trade lanes. On the Transpacific, Asia-US West Coast increased 1.92% to 7,724.52, compared with 7,579.09 a week earlier. Asia-US East Coast rose 1.89% to 10,125.18 from 9,936.89. Both routes therefore recorded further gains, extending the positive movement on the West Coast and reversing the marginal decline previously recorded on the East Coast. Asia-North Europe increased 5.40% to 3,203.78 from 3,039.67, marking a recovery following several consecutive weekly declines. The Transatlantic market also returned to positive territory. Westbound rates increased 2.19% to 2,945.35 from 2,882.09, reversing the previous week’s decrease. Eastbound rates recorded the largest percentage increase among the five NYFI routes, surging 18.77% to 1,124.31 from 946.64. The Eastbound recovery followed a particularly sharp decline of 19.28% in the preceding assessment, illustrating the considerable short-term volatility affecting the route. Drewry WCI declines as Transpacific rates weaken Drewry’s WCI declined 3% to US$4,429 per 40-foot container in its assessment published on 29 October, reversing two consecutive weekly increases. The decline was primarily driven by weaker Transpacific freight rates. Shanghai-Los Angeles decreased 6% to US$7,514 per 40-foot container, while Shanghai-New York fell 5% to US$9,631. According to Drewry, six blank sailings had been announced for the following week on the Transpacific, compared with five in the current week. The consultancy also highlighted expectations of weaker US import demand, citing a National Retail Federation forecast indicating an 11% month-on-month decline in US ocean import volumes during November. On Asia-Europe, the picture was more stable. Shanghai-Rotterdam increased 1% to US$3,686 per 40-foot container, while Shanghai-Genoa remained unchanged at US$4,151. Drewry reported four announced blank sailings for the following week on Asia-Europe services, compared with eight in the current week. Although carriers have announced higher Freight All Kinds (FAK) rates for November, the consultancy noted uncertainty over whether these increases can be sustained amid available capacity and weak demand. FBX Global Index slips 1% The FBX Global Container Freight Index declined 1% to US$3,513, compared with US$3,560 in the previous assessment. The decrease followed two consecutive weekly increases, including a 5% rise in the preceding reading. The latest movement places the FBX alongside Drewry’s WCI in negative territory, contrasting with the marginal increases recorded by the SCFI and CCFI. Transpacific assessments show contrasting trends One of the most notable developments in the latest readings is the difference between the Transpacific movements reported by NYFI and Drewry. NYFI recorded increases of 1.92% on Asia-US West Coast and 1.89% on Asia-US East Coast. Drewry, however, reported declines of 6% on Shanghai-Los Angeles and 5% on Shanghai-New York. The differing movements should be interpreted in the context of each index’s methodology, route coverage and reporting periods. NYFI is based on freight rates associated with containers that have actually shipped, while Drewry’s WCI assesses spot freight rates across selected trade lanes. Consequently, the two benchmarks can capture different market developments within broadly comparable trading regions. On Asia-Europe, the latest assessments were more closely aligned. NYFI Asia-North Europe increased 5.40%, while Drewry’s Shanghai-Rotterdam route advanced 1% and Shanghai-Genoa remained stable. Market outlook The latest figures indicate that container freight rate developments remain uneven across global trade lanes. Drewry’s WCI and the FBX declined, while the three Chinese composite benchmarks showed comparatively small movements. At the same time, NYFI recorded increases across all five monitored routes, including a notable rebound on Asia-North Europe and a sharp recovery on Transatlantic Eastbound. Looking ahead, the Transpacific market will remain particularly important as Drewry anticipates further downward pressure amid expectations of softer US import demand. On Asia-Europe, the effectiveness of announced November FAK increases and carriers’ capacity adjustments will be important factors to monitor. For now, the latest assessments highlight a market in which the direction of freight rates depends heavily on the benchmark and trade lane being examined.

articles.body: News Top Right Ernst Russ sells 803 TEU containership November 3, 2026 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Email MIRROR; Source: VesselFinder Ernst Russ AG has agreed to sell the 803 TEU containership Mirror , with delivery to its new owner scheduled for January 2027. The Hamburg-based shipowner did not disclose the sale price or identify the buyer. As the handover will take place next year, the transaction will not affect the company’s assets, financial position or earnings for the 2026 financial year. The vessel was built in 2007. Its sale follows Ernst Russ’ disposal of the containerships EF Emira and EF Emma earlier in 2026. During the same period, the company expanded its exposure to multipurpose vessels and product and chemical tankers. Its latest fleet addition was the newbuild tanker Farrie Russ , which was delivered on 27 October 2026. “The sale of MV Mirror reflects the disciplined approach we take in developing the Ernst Russ AG fleet,” said Joseph Schuchmann, Co-CEO and Chief Commercial Officer of Ernst Russ AG. “This includes parting with existing vessels at the right time and adding new tonnage just as selectively. We continuously monitor the market and assess both sale and acquisition opportunities,” he added.
